newsitem.title: UK: LME nickel sinks to five-month low in pre-market.
newsitem.headline: LME nickel sinks to five-month low in pre-market.

text.p: Nickel prices sank to the lowest level since January early on Monday, after coming under heavy selling pressure last week.
Three months London Metal Exchange (LME) nickel was last indicated at $7,050/$7,075 per tonne, versus a kerb close on Friday of $7,200.
The break below important support at $7,110 suggested prices could test the next support level at $6,940 if speculative selling continued to pile in, chartists said.
Selling said to have originated in a large U.S. investment bank started a downward spiral in nickel prices last week.
Traders said a tentative agreement on a new three-year contract reached on Friday between Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd and unionised workers at its Ontario division had also undermined the market.
The union had set a strike deadline for midnight Saturday.
